prompt: When must you have your driver license with you?
choices: Only when you drive outside your home state
Any time you are driving
Only when you drive someone else's vehicle
Only during your first year of driving
explanation: You must have your license with you whenever you drive and show it to a police officer who asks for it. The rule is not limited to trips out of state or to new drivers.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., FL p. 9, GA p. 8, AK p. 77)

prompt: Can a learner permit holder legally drive alone?
choices: Yes, during daylight hours on roads they know well
Yes, if they stay on local streets near home
No, a qualified licensed driver must ride with them
Yes, once they have passed the knowledge test
explanation: A learner permit lets you practice only while supervised by a licensed driver who meets your state's requirements. Passing the knowledge test is how you get the permit; it does not let you drive alone.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., FL p. 9, NY p. 13)

prompt: A police car behind you turns on its flashing lights and siren. What should you do?
choices: Signal and pull to the right as soon as it is safe
Stop right away in your lane, wherever you are
Keep driving at the same speed until you reach home
Speed up and let the officer pass you on the left
explanation: Signal to show the officer you have seen them, then move to the right and stop as soon as you can do so safely. Stopping suddenly in a traffic lane can cause a crash.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CA p. 35, CO p. 22, TX p. 71)

prompt: You have been pulled over by a police officer. Where should you and your passengers wait?
choices: Outside the car, next to the driver's door
Walking back toward the patrol car
Standing on the shoulder behind your car
Inside the car unless told to get out
explanation: Stay inside your vehicle during a traffic stop unless the officer tells you to get out. Getting out and walking toward the officer can be dangerous and alarming.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CA p. 35, CO p. 22, NJ p. 83)

prompt: While an officer walks up to your stopped car, what should you do with your hands?
choices: Dig through the glove box so your papers are ready
Keep them in view, such as on the steering wheel
Keep them in your lap, below the window
Reach under the seat to get your wallet ready
explanation: Keep your hands in plain view, such as on top of the steering wheel, and avoid sudden movements. Wait for the officer to ask before reaching for documents.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., TX p. 71, NJ p. 83, AK p. 77)

prompt: Does a state identification (ID) card allow you to drive?
choices: Yes, if it shows your photo and address
Yes, but only with a licensed adult in the car
No, an ID card is for identification only
Yes, for short trips near home
explanation: An ID card proves who you are but does not give you any driving privilege. To drive, you need a valid driver license or learner permit.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CA p. 7)

prompt: Which statement best describes driving on public roads?
choices: It is a privilege that can be suspended or revoked
It is a right that cannot be taken away once you have a license
It is a right that every adult has, with or without a license
It is a right guaranteed to anyone who passes the driving test
explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. You earn it by meeting the licensing rules, and the state can suspend or revoke it if you break serious traffic laws.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., AK p. 9, MI p. 11, PA p. 3, NJ p. 2)

prompt: What does it mean when your driver license is suspended?
choices: You may drive only during the day
You may drive only if you carry the suspension notice
You may drive, but you will pay a higher fine if stopped
Your privilege to drive is taken away for a time
explanation: A suspension temporarily takes away your privilege to drive. You may not legally drive until the privilege is restored, and driving while suspended brings further penalties.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., TX p. 81, AZ p. 62, NE p. 25)

prompt: What is a "hit-and-run"?
choices: A crash in which one car hits the back of another
Leaving a crash scene without stopping as the law requires
Hitting a parked car while backing up
A crash that happens while a driver is running a red light
explanation: Failing to stop, or leaving the scene of a crash you were involved in, is called a hit-and-run. It is against the law, and the penalties are severe, especially when someone is hurt.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CA p. 83, NY p. 77, FL p. 85)

prompt: During a traffic stop, the officer asks for your license, which is in a backpack on the back seat. What should you do?
choices: Tell the officer where it is and wait for permission before reaching for it
Quickly turn around and grab the backpack before the officer asks again
Get out of the car and open the back door to get it
Say you do not have it so you can avoid reaching around
explanation: Tell the officer where your documents are and wait for the officer's okay before you reach for them. Sudden reaching can look like you are grabbing something dangerous.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CO p. 22, TX p. 71, NJ p. 83)

prompt: You are pulled over by police at night. Which action helps make the stop safer?
choices: Turn on your high beams so you can see the officer
Get out of the car so the officer can see you
Turn on the interior light so the officer can see inside the car
Turn off all of your lights so you do not blind the officer
explanation: At night, turn on your interior (dome) light so the officer can see inside your vehicle. This reduces uncertainty for the officer and helps the stop go smoothly.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CO p. 22, TX p. 71, NJ p. 83, AK p. 77)

prompt: A friend who does not have a driver license asks to drive your car around the block. What should you do?
choices: Let them, as long as you ride along with them
Let them, because it is only a short distance
Let them, as long as your car's registration is current
Say no; letting an unlicensed person drive is illegal
explanation: It is illegal to let an unlicensed person drive your vehicle, even for a short trip. Riding along does not make it legal unless they hold a learner permit and you meet the supervisor rules.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., FL p. 3, FL p. 33)

prompt: Your cousin, who looks a lot like you, wants to borrow your driver license for a weekend trip. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, if your cousin is a careful driver
No, lending your license is illegal
Yes, if your cousin is over 18 and insured
Yes, if your cousin only drives your car
explanation: Your license may be used only by you. Lending it to someone else, or using someone else's license, is illegal and can cost you your driving privilege.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., TX p. 17, AZ p. 65)

prompt: Your vehicle registration expired last week, but you never got a renewal notice in the mail. Which is true?
choices: It is fine to keep driving until a notice arrives
Registration only matters if you drive out of state
You are responsible for renewing on time, even without a reminder
An expired registration is fine as long as your license is valid
explanation: The vehicle owner is responsible for knowing when the registration expires and renewing it on time. Not getting a reminder is not an excuse, and a valid driver license does not cover an expired registration.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., NY p. 26, NJ p. 160)

prompt: You want to put a dark tinted cover over your license plate. Is that allowed?
choices: No, the plate must stay clearly readable
Yes, as long as the plate can be read in daylight
Yes, as long as your registration is current
Yes, if the cover came from a car dealer
explanation: License plates must be kept clean, visible and readable at all times. Covers or frames that hide or darken the letters and numbers are not allowed.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., NJ p. 161, NC p. 99)

prompt: You move to a new address in the same state. What must you do?
choices: Nothing until it is time to renew your license
Tell the post office, which updates your license record
Update your address only if you move to a new county
Report it to the licensing agency by your state's deadline
explanation: When you move, you must report your new address to the driver licensing agency within your state's deadline. Telling only the post office does not update your driver record.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CA p. 14, TX p. 15, NY p. 17, FL p. 20)

prompt: You move permanently to a new state. What should you do about your driver license?
choices: Keep using your old license until it expires
Get a license from your new state within the time its law allows
Carry both your old license and a new one at all times
Do nothing as long as you register your car in the new state
explanation: Once you become a resident of a new state, you must get that state's license within the period its law allows, usually by turning in your old one. Visitors may drive on a valid home-state license, but new residents may not keep doing so indefinitely.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., NY p. 18, TX p. 7)

prompt: You have a regular car license. A friend offers to let you ride their motorcycle on a public street. Which is true?
choices: You may ride it, because a car license covers all vehicle types
You may ride it if you stay under the speed limit
You need a motorcycle license or endorsement
You may ride it if your friend rides behind you
explanation: You must hold the correct license class for the vehicle you drive. A regular car license does not let you ride a motorcycle on public roads; you need a motorcycle license or endorsement.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CA p. 7, TX p. 7, NY p. 7)

prompt: During a traffic stop, the officer asks you to step out of your car. What should you do?
choices: Refuse, because drivers should always stay inside
Get out quickly and walk toward the officer with your wallet in hand
Reach under your seat for your papers before you get out
Step out carefully, watching traffic, with hands visible
explanation: If the officer asks you to get out, do so carefully, watch for traffic, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs. Staying inside is the rule only until the officer tells you otherwise.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CO p. 22, GA p. 5, TX p. 71)

prompt: A friend offers to change the birth date on your driver license so you look older. What is true?
choices: It is illegal and can cost you your license
It is legal if you do not use it to drive
It is only a problem if a police officer notices
It is legal as long as the photo is still yours
explanation: Changing any information on a license, or showing a license you know is altered or fake, is illegal. It can lead to suspension of your driving privilege and other penalties.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., AZ p. 65, TX p. 17)

prompt: Another driver runs a red light and hits your car. The damage to your car is small. What must you do?
choices: Leave, because the crash was not your fault
Stop and exchange the required information
Leave, because the damage is too small to matter
Drive home first and call the other driver later
explanation: Every driver involved in a crash must stop, no matter who caused it, and exchange the required information. Being the innocent driver does not excuse you from staying at the scene.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CA p. 83, NY p. 77, TX p. 65)

prompt: You are in the far left lane of a four-lane highway when a police car signals you to stop. The left shoulder is wide. What should you usually do?
choices: Stop on the left shoulder because it is closer
Stop in the left lane and turn on your hazard lights
Signal and move safely to the right, unless told otherwise
Take the next exit and drive to the nearest police station
explanation: Even from the left lane, signal and move to the right side of the road when it is safe, unless the officer tells you otherwise. Officers expect drivers to pull to the right, and stopping in a lane is dangerous.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., AK p. 77, CA p. 35)

prompt: Late at night on a dark, empty road, an unmarked car with flashing lights signals you to stop, and you are not sure it is a real officer. What is a reasonable way to respond?
choices: Speed up and try to lose the car before it reaches you
Stop right away on the dark shoulder and get out to check
Ignore the lights and keep driving at normal speed until you get home
Turn on your flashers, slow down and drive to a well-lit public place
explanation: Show the officer you are cooperating by turning on your hazard lights and slowing down, then stop at a nearby well-lit, busy place. You can call 911 to confirm the officer is real. Fleeing or ignoring the lights can lead to arrest.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., TX p. 71, IL p. 24, AR p. 3)

prompt: An officer gives you a ticket you believe is unfair. What is the right way to handle it?
choices: Stay calm and contest it later in court
Argue until the officer agrees to cancel it
Refuse to take the ticket and drive away
Get out of the car to explain your side face to face
explanation: If you disagree with an officer, stay calm and respectful and do not argue at the roadside. You can contest the ticket in court through the normal legal process.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., CO p. 22, GA p. 5, FL p. 84, NE p. 36)

prompt: You panic after a minor crash and drive away. A block later you realize what you did. What should you do?
choices: Go home and wait to see if anyone contacts you
Go back to the scene right away
Call your insurance company and let it report the crash
Nothing, because the damage was minor
explanation: If you failed to stop after a crash you were involved in, you must go back to the scene right away and meet your legal duties. Staying away turns the crash into a hit-and-run.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., TX p. 65, CA p. 83, NY p. 77)

prompt: You have a learner permit. Your licensed parent says you can drive alone to a store two blocks away. What is true?
choices: It is legal because your parent gave permission
It is legal because the trip is short
It is illegal without a supervisor in the car
It is legal as long as you carry your permit
explanation: A permit holder may drive only with a qualified licensed supervisor in the vehicle. A parent's permission does not replace the supervisor's presence, no matter how short the trip.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., FL p. 9, NY p. 13)

prompt: You know your friend's license is suspended, but you let him borrow your car anyway. If he is caught driving it, who can face penalties?
choices: Only your friend, because he was the one driving
Only you, because you own the car
No one, as long as the car's registration is current
Your friend for driving, and you for allowing it
explanation: Driving while suspended is illegal, and so is knowingly letting someone without a valid license drive your vehicle. As the owner, you can be penalized too.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g., FL p. 3, FL p. 33)
